Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১) The drug sibutramine is used in.........?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Sibutramine is a centrally acting appetite suppressant that was formerly used for the management of obesity. It inhibits the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin (and to a lesser extent dopamine) in the hypothalamus, increasing satiety and reducing food intake. However, sibutramine was withdrawn from many markets because it was associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events, including myocardial infarction and stroke, particularly in patients with cardiovascular disease. Therefore, among the given options, obesity is the correct indication. It is not used for smoking cessation, hypothermia, or pellagra.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sibutramine → appetite suppressant → obesity

  • Mechanism: inhibits norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake

  • Increases satiety and decreases food intake.

  • Important adverse effects: increased blood pressure and heart rate

  • Withdrawn/restricted in many countries because of cardiovascular risk.

Exam Pearl: Sibutramine is an anti-obesity drug that suppresses appetite by inhibiting monoamine reuptake.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২) Which is first neurotrophin to be characterized?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Nerve growth factor (NGF) was the first neurotrophin to be characterized. It was discovered through studies of factors that promote the survival and growth of sympathetic and sensory neurons. NGF is particularly important for the development, survival, and maintenance of sensory neurons and sympathetic neurons. Other major neurotrophins were characterized later: BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor), NT-3 (neurotrophin-3), and NT-4/5 (neurotrophin-4/5). NGF exerts its principal effects through the high-affinity TrkA receptor, while mature NGF can also interact with the p75 neurotrophin receptor.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • First neurotrophin characterized → NGF

  • NGF → survival of sympathetic and sensory neurons

  • NGF high-affinity receptor → TrkA

  • BDNF → primarily signals through TrkB

  • NT-3 → primarily signals through TrkC

Exam Pearl: NGF was the first identified and characterized neurotrophin.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩) Structure subject to barotrauma includes....?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Barotrauma is tissue injury caused by a difference between the pressure of an enclosed gas-filled space and the surrounding environmental pressure, commonly occurring during diving or rapid changes in altitude. The paranasal sinuses are classic air-containing spaces susceptible to barotrauma, particularly when their drainage openings are obstructed. Pressure differences can cause mucosal edema, pain, bleeding, or sinus injury. The middle ear is also a very important and commonly tested site of barotrauma, but it is not explicitly listed among the options. The inner ear is fluid-filled and is less directly affected by pressure changes than the middle ear. Therefore, among the given options, sinuses is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sinuses → susceptible to barotrauma

  • Middle ear → most common site of barotrauma

  • Common during scuba diving and rapid altitude changes

  • Blocked sinus ostia increase the risk of sinus barotrauma.

  • Pressure-related injury can cause pain, mucosal edema, and hemorrhage.

Exam Pearl: Think air-filled spaces: middle ear and paranasal sinuses are classic sites of barotrauma.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪) Features of pyramidal tract lesion excludes…?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).option4: Loss of performance of fine skilled movements
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A pyramidal (corticospinal) tract lesion typically produces upper motor neuron (UMN) signs. These include spastic weakness, an extensor plantar response (Babinski sign), increased muscle tone with a clasp-knife phenomenon, and impairment of fine, skilled voluntary movements. Flaccid paralysis is primarily a feature of a lower motor neuron (LMN) lesion, particularly when the lesion affects the anterior horn cells, peripheral nerves, or motor roots. In the acute phase of a severe UMN lesion, however, there may be transient flaccidity due to spinal shock, but this is not the typical established feature of a pyramidal tract lesion. Therefore, the best answer is flaccid paralysis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • UMN lesion → spasticity

  • UMN lesion → Babinski sign

  • UMN lesion → clasp-knife phenomenon

  • UMN lesion → loss of fine skilled movements

  • LMN lesion → flaccid paralysis, fasciculations, muscle wasting, reduced reflexes

Exam Pearl: Pyramidal lesion = UMN signs; flaccidity is classically an LMN feature.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫) What is the cause of rusty sputum?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Rusty sputum is a classic clinical feature of pneumococcal pneumonia, most commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. The rusty or reddish-brown appearance results from blood mixed with inflammatory exudate within the alveoli. Classically, pneumococcal pneumonia may progress through stages of congestion, red hepatization, gray hepatization, and resolution, with hemoptysis contributing to the characteristic sputum. Pulmonary edema typically produces pink, frothy sputum, while bronchiectasis commonly causes copious purulent sputum and may be associated with hemoptysis. Cystic fibrosis produces recurrent respiratory infections with thick, purulent secretions rather than classically rusty sputum.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rusty sputum → pneumococcal pneumonia

  • Pneumococcus → Streptococcus pneumoniae

  • Pulmonary edema → pink, frothy sputum

  • Bronchiectasis → copious purulent sputum

  • Rusty sputum is associated with alveolar inflammation and blood admixture.

Exam Pearl: Rusty sputum is a classic exam clue for pneumococcal pneumonia.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬) Which means extend, direction & weight of movement?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Kinesthetic sensation is the sensory modality that provides information about the position and movement of body parts, including the direction, extent, and force/weight of movement. It arises mainly from proprioceptors in muscles, tendons, and joints. Muscle spindles provide information about muscle length and change in length, while Golgi tendon organs provide information about muscle tension. In contrast, tactile localization refers to identifying the precise location of a touch, tactile discrimination involves distinguishing two or more tactile stimuli, and vibration sense detects high-frequency mechanical oscillations. Therefore, the description of knowing the extent, direction, and weight of movement best corresponds to kinesthetic sensation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Kinesthesia → sense of movement

  • Proprioception → position and movement of body parts

  • Muscle spindle → muscle length/stretch

  • Golgi tendon organ → muscle tension

  • Vibration sense → mainly mediated by large myelinated fibers

Exam Pearl: Kinesthetic sensation tells you how a limb is moving—its direction, extent, and force.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭) Pellagra doesn't include which of the following?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pellagra results from niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency and classically presents with the “3 Ds” — Dermatitis, Diarrhoea, and Dementia. Dermatitis is typically photosensitive and may occur on exposed areas of the skin. Gastrointestinal involvement causes diarrhoea, while neurological involvement can produce cognitive impairment, confusion, and ultimately dementia. Delirium is not one of the classic three manifestations and therefore is the best answer to the question. Although severe pellagra can cause various neuropsychiatric manifestations, the standard exam association is the triad of dermatitis, diarrhoea, and dementia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pellagra → Niacin (B3) deficiency

  • Classic 3 Ds:

    • Dermatitis

    • Diarrhoea

    • Dementia

  • Severe untreated disease may progress to death.

  • Niacin deficiency can occur in malnutrition, alcoholism, and malabsorption.

Exam Pearl: Remember pellagra by the 3 Ds: Dermatitis + Diarrhoea + Dementia.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮) Conditions when tendon reflexes are absent excludes..?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Absent tendon reflexes are characteristic of conditions affecting the lower motor neuron, peripheral nerves, or sensory afferent pathways. In tabes dorsalis, degeneration of the dorsal roots and posterior columns leads to loss of deep tendon reflexes, classically producing Argyll Robertson pupils and sensory ataxia. Poliomyelitis damages anterior horn cells, producing lower motor neuron weakness with reduced or absent reflexes. Peripheral neuropathies commonly impair the reflex arc and therefore cause reduced or absent tendon reflexes. In contrast, tetanus causes generalized muscle rigidity and painful spasms, with reflexes generally preserved or sometimes exaggerated rather than characteristically absent.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Absent reflexes → LMN/peripheral nerve/sensory afferent lesion

  • Tabes dorsalis → sensory ataxia + absent reflexes

  • Poliomyelitis → anterior horn cell destruction

  • Peripheral neuropathy → reduced/absent reflexes

  • Tetanus → muscle rigidity + spasms

Exam Pearl: Absent tendon reflex = think LMN, peripheral nerve, or sensory afferent pathway; tetanus is not a classic cause.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯) Reduced cerebral perfusion in elderly people is manifested by......?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Reduced cerebral perfusion in older adults, particularly due to orthostatic hypotension, commonly manifests as lightheadedness or presyncope. When cerebral blood flow temporarily falls, patients may describe a sensation of faintness, weakness, or “about to pass out,” especially after standing. Vertigo specifically indicates an illusion of movement or spinning and usually suggests a vestibular or central neurological disorder rather than simple cerebral hypoperfusion. Unsteadiness and poor balance are more commonly associated with disorders of the vestibular system, cerebellum, proprioception, or musculoskeletal function. Therefore, among the options, lightheadedness is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Reduced cerebral perfusion → lightheadedness/presyncope

  • Orthostatic hypotension → dizziness or faintness on standing

  • Vertigo → illusion of movement/spinning

  • Cerebellar dysfunction → ataxia and unsteadiness

  • Vestibular dysfunction → vertigo and imbalance

Exam Pearl: Cerebral hypoperfusion classically causes lightheadedness/presyncope, not true vertigo.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০) Which nuclei lies in the lateral zone of hypothalamus?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The tuberomammillary nucleus (TMN) is located in the lateral part of the posterior hypothalamus and is the principal source of histamine-containing neurons in the brain. It plays an important role in wakefulness and arousal. The hypothalamus can be broadly described in medial and lateral zones, although individual nuclei are often grouped according to anterior–posterior regions as well. The paraventricular nucleus is mainly in the anterior/medial hypothalamus, while the infundibular (arcuate) nucleus lies in the mediobasal hypothalamus. The posterior nucleus is located in the posterior hypothalamic region but is not the classic answer for the lateral zone. Therefore, tuberomammillary nucleus is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tuberomammillary nucleus → lateral/posterior hypothalamus

  • TMN neurons → release histamine

  • Histamine from TMN → promotes wakefulness

  • Paraventricular nucleus → ADH/oxytocin synthesis and autonomic functions

  • Infundibular (arcuate) nucleus → hypothalamic endocrine regulation

Exam Pearl: Tuberomammillary nucleus = hypothalamic histamine center = wakefulness.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১১) Which is not caused by infective endocarditis?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Infective endocarditis (IE) produces several peripheral vascular and immunological manifestations. Digital clubbing may occur, particularly in subacute or prolonged infective endocarditis. Splinter hemorrhages are small linear hemorrhages under the nails and are a classic peripheral sign of IE. Systemic embolism can occur when infected vegetations detach and travel through the systemic circulation, potentially causing stroke, renal or splenic infarction, or limb ischemia. Central cyanosis, however, is not a typical manifestation of infective endocarditis. Central cyanosis reflects increased deoxygenated hemoglobin in arterial blood and is generally caused by significant hypoxemia or right-to-left shunting. Therefore, central cyanosis is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • IE → splinter hemorrhages

  • IE → digital clubbing may occur in prolonged disease

  • IE → systemic embolization from vegetations

  • IE → Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, Roth spots

  • Central cyanosis → think hypoxemia or right-to-left shunt

Exam Pearl: Central cyanosis is not a classic peripheral manifestation of infective endocarditis.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১২) Secretion from seminal vesicle contributes …..% of volume of semen?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The seminal vesicles contribute approximately 60% of the total volume of semen, making them the largest contributor among the accessory sex glands. Their secretion is an alkaline, fructose-rich fluid that provides an important energy source for spermatozoa. It also contains prostaglandins and coagulating proteins that contribute to semen function. The prostate contributes approximately 25–30%, while the testes/epididymal contribution is relatively small. Therefore, among the given options, 60% is the accepted exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Seminal vesicles → ~60% of semen volume

  • Seminal vesicle secretion → fructose-rich

  • Fructose → energy source for sperm

  • Prostate → approximately 25–30%

  • Seminal vesicles are the largest contributor to semen volume

Exam Pearl: Seminal vesicles contribute about 60% of semen volume.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৩) Withdrawal of beta blocker abruptly may precipitate....?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Abrupt withdrawal of a beta-blocker can cause rebound sympathetic activity because chronic beta-blockade leads to increased beta-adrenergic receptor sensitivity. Sudden discontinuation may therefore produce tachycardia, increased myocardial contractility, and increased myocardial oxygen demand. In patients with ischemic heart disease, this can precipitate worsening angina, including unstable angina, and may increase the risk of myocardial infarction or sudden cardiac events. Beta-blockers should therefore generally be tapered rather than stopped abruptly, particularly in patients with coronary artery disease. Asthma and COPD are not the classic complications of beta-blocker withdrawal, while myocarditis is unrelated to withdrawal.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Abrupt beta-blocker withdrawal → rebound sympathetic activity

  • May cause tachycardia and increased myocardial oxygen demand

  • Can precipitate angina/MI

  • Particularly important in patients with ischemic heart disease

  • Beta-blockers should generally be tapered gradually

Exam Pearl: Never abruptly stop a beta-blocker in a patient with coronary disease—rebound sympathetic activity can precipitate unstable angina or MI.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৪) Which is not a chromosomal disorder of sex differentiation?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Turner syndrome (45,X), Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), and super male syndrome (47,XYY) are chromosomal abnormalities involving sex chromosomes and can cause disorders of sex development. In contrast, pseudohermaphroditism is primarily a disorder of sexual differentiation in which the external genitalia do not correspond to the individual's chromosomal/gonadal sex, often due to abnormalities of hormone production, metabolism, or action. Examples include androgen insensitivity syndrome and congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Therefore, among the given options, pseudohermaphroditism is not itself a chromosomal disorder.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Turner syndrome → 45,X

  • Klinefelter syndrome → 47,XXY

  • Super male → 47,XYY

  • Pseudohermaphroditism → discrepancy between chromosomal/gonadal sex and external phenotype

  • Androgen insensitivity → 46,XY with androgen receptor dysfunction

Exam Pearl: Turner, Klinefelter, and XYY are chromosomal disorders; pseudohermaphroditism is a disorder of sexual differentiation, not a specific chromosomal abnormality.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৫) Deficiency of which vitamin may causes high output cardiac failure?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency can cause wet beriberi, which may present with high-output cardiac failure. Thiamine is required as a cofactor for several enzymes involved in carbohydrate metabolism, including pyruvate dehydrogenase and transketolase. Severe deficiency impairs energy production and causes peripheral vasodilation, leading to reduced systemic vascular resistance. The resulting increase in venous return and cardiac workload can produce a high-output state, eventually progressing to cardiac failure with edema and tachycardia. This cardiovascular manifestation is classically called wet beriberi. Niacin deficiency causes pellagra, menaquinone is vitamin K2, and biotin deficiency is associated mainly with dermatitis, alopecia, and neurological manifestations.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thiamine deficiency → wet beriberi

  • Wet beriberi → high-output cardiac failure

  • Thiamine → cofactor in carbohydrate metabolism

  • Severe deficiency → peripheral vasodilation and reduced SVR

  • Dry beriberi → predominantly peripheral neuropathy

Exam Pearl: High-output cardiac failure + vitamin deficiency = think thiamine (B1) deficiency.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৬) Which is the feature of latent tetany?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Latent tetany occurs when neuromuscular excitability is increased, usually because of hypocalcaemia, but spontaneous muscle spasms are not yet present. The classic clinical signs are Trousseau's sign and Chvostek's sign. Trousseau's sign is elicited by inflating a blood-pressure cuff above systolic pressure for several minutes, producing carpopedal spasm in a patient with latent tetany. In contrast, carpopedal spasm, stridor from laryngospasm, and convulsions represent more overt manifestations of significant hypocalcaemia/tetany. Therefore, Trousseau's sign is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Latent tetany → Trousseau's sign

  • Chvostek's sign → facial muscle twitching after facial nerve stimulation

  • Hypocalcaemia → increased neuromuscular excitability

  • Severe hypocalcaemia → laryngospasm, seizures, carpopedal spasm

  • Trousseau's sign is generally more specific for latent tetany than Chvostek's sign

Exam Pearl: Latent tetany is classically demonstrated by Trousseau's sign.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৭) Which of the following case is to be treated under category-1 anti-TB treatment regimen?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In the traditional WHO/RNTCP-style TB classification, Category I treatment was used for new patients with severe forms of tuberculosis, including severe extrapulmonary TB such as TB meningitis, miliary TB, or other serious disseminated disease. The standard Category I regimen was 2 months of HRZE followed by 4 months of HR. In contrast, relapse, treatment failure, and treatment after default were historically classified under Category II, which used an extended regimen including streptomycin. Therefore, among the given options, severe extra-pulmonary TB is the best answer. Modern TB programs increasingly use drug-susceptibility testing and drug-resistant TB–specific regimens rather than the old Category I/II framework.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Traditional Category I → new severe TB cases

  • Severe extrapulmonary TB → Category I

  • Relapse → traditionally Category II

  • Treatment failure → traditionally Category II

  • Treatment after default → traditionally Category II

  • Modern TB management → increasingly based on drug susceptibility and resistance pattern

Exam Pearl: In the traditional Category I/II system, severe extrapulmonary TB belongs to Category I.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৮) What is the molecular weight of calcitonin?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Calcitonin is a peptide hormone produced by the parafollicular (C) cells of the thyroid gland. Human calcitonin consists of 32 amino acids and has a molecular mass of approximately 3.4 kDa (about 3,400 Da). Among the options provided, 3,200 Da is the closest and is the traditionally accepted value used in some examination sources. Calcitonin primarily acts to lower plasma calcium concentration, mainly by inhibiting osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. It also promotes renal calcium and phosphate excretion. Because none of the options gives the approximate molecular mass of 3,400 Da, the question is slightly imperfect; 3,200 Da is the best available answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Calcitonin → produced by thyroid C cells

  • Human calcitonin → 32 amino acids

  • Molecular mass → approximately 3.4 kDa

  • Main action → decreases serum Ca²⁺

  • Inhibits osteoclast activity

Exam Pearl: Calcitonin is a 32-amino-acid peptide with a molecular mass of roughly 3.4 kDa.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৯) What will be the percussion note in case of pleural effusion?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In pleural effusion, fluid accumulates in the pleural cavity and replaces the normally air-filled space around the lung. On percussion, this produces a characteristic stony dull note over the area of significant effusion. Stony dullness is more marked than the ordinary dullness found over solid lung tissue, such as in lobar consolidation. A resonant note is normally heard over healthy aerated lung. Woody dullness is classically associated with marked consolidation or other conditions producing very dense underlying tissue, depending on the clinical context. Therefore, stony dullness is the classic examination finding in pleural effusion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pleural effusion → stony dull percussion note

  • Consolidation → dull

  • Normal lung → resonant

  • Pneumothorax → hyperresonant

  • Pleural effusion → reduced/absent breath sounds over the fluid

Exam Pearl: Pleural fluid = stony dull percussion note.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২০) Which is not growth promoting hormone?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cortisol is not considered a growth-promoting hormone. In fact, excess glucocorticoids inhibit growth, particularly in children, by suppressing growth hormone secretion and action, reducing IGF-1 activity, and inhibiting protein synthesis and bone/cartilage growth. In contrast, growth hormone (GH) directly promotes linear growth through IGF-1. Thyroid hormones are essential for normal growth and skeletal maturation and also support GH action. Androgens promote growth during puberty, initially accelerating the growth spurt, although they eventually contribute to epiphyseal closure. Therefore, cortisol is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • GH → major growth-promoting hormone

  • Thyroid hormone → essential for normal growth and development

  • Androgens → pubertal growth spurt

  • Cortisol excess → growth retardation

  • Excess glucocorticoids → suppress GH/IGF-1-mediated growth

Exam Pearl: Cortisol is anti-growth when excessive; GH, thyroid hormones, and sex steroids support normal growth.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২১) A patient present with chronic cough, productive copious purulent sputum, digital clubbing, coarse crepitation. What is the best possible diagnosis?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The combination of chronic productive cough, copious purulent sputum, digital clubbing, and coarse crepitations is highly characteristic of bronchiectasis. Bronchiectasis is a chronic condition involving permanent abnormal dilatation of the bronchi, usually resulting from recurrent infection and impaired mucociliary clearance. Patients classically produce large amounts of foul-smelling or purulent sputum, often with recurrent infective exacerbations. On auscultation, coarse crackles are commonly heard, particularly over the affected areas. Digital clubbing may occur in longstanding or severe disease. Lung abscess typically presents with fever and a localized cavity with foul sputum, while bronchial carcinoma may cause clubbing but does not classically produce copious purulent sputum with widespread coarse crepitations. Pulmonary tuberculosis usually presents with chronic cough, fever, weight loss, and sometimes hemoptysis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bronchiectasis → copious purulent sputum

  • Digital clubbing may occur

  • Auscultation → coarse crackles/crepitations

  • Caused by permanent bronchial dilatation

  • Recurrent infections are common

  • Hemoptysis can occur due to bronchial artery hypertrophy

Exam Pearl: Chronic cough + copious purulent sputum + coarse crackles + clubbing = bronchiectasis.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২২) Hydroxyapatite crystal is a form of which mineral?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hydroxyapatite is the principal inorganic mineral component of bone and teeth. Chemically, it is a crystalline calcium phosphate compound with the formula Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂. Although it contains both calcium and phosphate, when asked which mineral hydroxyapatite is a form of, the accepted exam answer is calcium. Hydroxyapatite crystals provide the hardness and structural strength of bone, while the organic matrix, particularly type I collagen, provides tensile strength. Bone mineral is continuously remodeled through coordinated osteoclastic resorption and osteoblastic formation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hydroxyapatite → major bone mineral

  • Composition → calcium + phosphate + hydroxyl

  • Formula → Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂

  • Type I collagen → major organic component of bone

  • Hydroxyapatite → provides bone hardness

Exam Pearl: Hydroxyapatite is a calcium phosphate mineral and the major inorganic component of bone.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৩) Which drug is used for Anti IgE therapy?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Omalizumab is a recombinant humanized monoclonal antibody directed against immunoglobulin E (IgE). It binds circulating free IgE and prevents IgE from binding to high-affinity FcεRI receptors on mast cells and basophils, thereby reducing allergic inflammatory responses. It is used primarily in moderate-to-severe persistent allergic asthma that remains inadequately controlled with standard therapy, and it also has established uses in conditions such as chronic spontaneous urticaria and nasal polyps in selected patients. Abciximab is an antiplatelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitor, adalimumab targets TNF-α, and rituximab targets CD20 on B cells.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anti-IgE → Omalizumab

  • Omalizumab → monoclonal antibody against free IgE

  • Reduces IgE-mediated activation of mast cells and basophils

  • Important use → allergic asthma

  • Adalimumab → anti-TNF-α

  • Rituximab → anti-CD20

Exam Pearl: Omalizumab = anti-IgE monoclonal antibody.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৪) Which one isn't a component of CURB-65 score to assess severity of pneumonia?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The CURB-65 score is used to assess the severity and mortality risk of community-acquired pneumonia. The acronym represents Confusion, Urea >7 mmol/L, Respiratory rate ≥30/min, Blood pressure <90 mmHg systolic or ≤60 mmHg diastolic, and age ≥65 years. Therefore, urea >5 mmol/L is not the standard CURB-65 criterion; the accepted threshold is >7 mmol/L. The other listed features—confusion, respiratory rate ≥30/min, and age ≥65 years—are genuine components. Thus, option B is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • C → Confusion

  • U → Urea > 7 mmol/L

  • R → Respiratory rate ≥ 30/min

  • B → BP <90 systolic or ≤60 diastolic

  • 65 → Age ≥65 years

  • Score 0–1 → generally lower risk; higher scores indicate increasing severity.

Exam Pearl: CURB-65: Urea cutoff is >7 mmol/L, not >5 mmol/L.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৫) Gastric erosions & ulcers are differentiated from each other on the basis of their penetration into.......?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The key histological distinction between a gastric erosion and a gastric ulcer is the depth of mucosal injury. A gastric erosion is a superficial defect that does not penetrate beyond the muscularis mucosae. In contrast, a true gastric ulcer extends through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa or deeper layers, and may reach the muscularis externa or even perforate the serosa. Therefore, strictly speaking, the defining distinction is penetration through the muscularis mucosae, not necessarily all the way to the muscularis externa. However, among the options provided, muscularis externa is the best exam answer because it represents a deeper penetrating lesion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Erosion → superficial mucosal defect

  • Ulcer → extends through muscularis mucosae

  • Gastric ulcer may extend into submucosa and muscularis externa

  • Perforation → may extend through the entire gastric wall

  • Muscularis mucosae is the key anatomical boundary distinguishing erosion from ulcer.

Exam Pearl: Erosion is superficial; a true ulcer penetrates beyond the muscularis mucosae.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৬) Which Epithelial cell junction is devoid of any Cytoskeletal components?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Gap junctions are specialized intercellular channels formed by connexins assembled into connexons. Unlike tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes, gap junctions do not have a cytoplasmic plaque or direct attachment to the cytoskeleton. Tight junctions interact with actin through proteins such as ZO-1, adherens junctions are linked to actin filaments through catenins, and desmosomes are anchored to intermediate filaments through desmosomal proteins. Gap junctions primarily allow direct passage of ions and small molecules between adjacent cells, enabling electrical and metabolic coupling. Therefore, gap junction is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gap junction → no direct cytoskeletal attachment

  • Gap junction proteins → connexins

  • Connexins form connexons

  • Adherens junction → actin

  • Desmosome → intermediate filaments

  • Tight junction → associated with actin cytoskeleton

Exam Pearl: Gap junctions are the epithelial junctions without a direct cytoskeletal anchorage.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৭) Inability to perform simple mental arithmetic tasks or draw objects such as stars found in hepatic encephalopathy is called....?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Constructional apraxia is the inability to construct or copy a visual-spatial figure despite adequate motor strength and comprehension. In hepatic encephalopathy, neuropsychiatric dysfunction can impair higher cortical functions, and patients may have difficulty performing tasks such as drawing a star or other simple figures and may also demonstrate impaired mental calculations. Asterixis is a different characteristic finding, consisting of brief, irregular lapses of sustained posture, producing a “flapping” movement, particularly with the hands outstretched. Hyperreflexia may occur in severe encephalopathy but is not the term for impaired drawing or calculation. Fetor hepaticus refers to the characteristic musty breath odor associated with advanced liver disease.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hepatic encephalopathy → constructional apraxia

  • Constructional apraxia → inability to copy/draw figures

  • Asterixis → flapping tremor

  • Fetor hepaticus → musty breath odor

  • Severe hepatic encephalopathy → altered consciousness and neurological signs

Exam Pearl: Difficulty drawing a star or simple figure in hepatic encephalopathy = constructional apraxia.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৮) Which hepatitis virus has window period?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The window period is the interval during acute infection when HBsAg has disappeared but anti-HBs has not yet become detectable. During this period, anti-HBc IgM is the key serological marker that indicates recent HBV infection. This classic “window period” is particularly associated with hepatitis B and is an important examination concept. Hepatitis A, C, and E do not classically have this characteristic serological window period described in standard HBV serology questions. Therefore, hepatitis B virus is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HBV → classic window period

  • Window period → HBsAg negative, anti-HBs not yet detectable

  • Key marker → IgM anti-HBc

  • HBsAg → indicates current HBV infection

  • Anti-HBs → indicates immunity/recovery

Exam Pearl: HBV window period = HBsAg disappears before anti-HBs appears; IgM anti-HBc remains positive.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৯) Which one of the following is a cause of malabsorption syndrome?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Coeliac disease is a classic cause of malabsorption syndrome due to an immune-mediated response to gluten, causing villous atrophy and crypt hyperplasia in the small intestine. This reduces the absorptive surface area and can lead to deficiencies of iron, folate, vitamin B12, calcium, and fat-soluble vitamins. Crohn's disease can also cause malabsorption, particularly when the small intestine or terminal ileum is extensively involved, so the question is somewhat broad. However, when a single classic cause of malabsorption syndrome is asked, coeliac disease is the best answer. Acute pancreatitis can cause transient pancreatic dysfunction but is not a classic primary cause of chronic malabsorption syndrome, while ulcerative colitis primarily affects the colon.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Coeliac disease → classic malabsorption syndrome

  • Pathology → villous atrophy

  • Trigger → gluten

  • Common deficiency → iron

  • Crohn's disease involving ileum → B12 and bile salt malabsorption

  • Steatorrhoea → suggests significant fat malabsorption

Exam Pearl: Coeliac disease is the classic exam answer for malabsorption syndrome.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩০) What is the commonest cause of upper GIT bleeding?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is the commonest cause of upper gastrointestinal (UGI) bleeding in standard clinical examination questions. Bleeding occurs when an ulcer erodes into a submucosal or larger arterial vessel, with the gastroduodenal artery being particularly important in posterior duodenal ulcers. Gastric erosions, oesophagitis, and vascular malformations can also cause upper GIT bleeding, but they are less common causes overall. Clinically, UGI bleeding may present with haematemesis, coffee-ground vomiting, and/or melaena. Important risk factors for ulcer-related bleeding include NSAID use, H. pylori infection, and anticoagulant therapy.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Commonest cause of UGI bleeding → Peptic ulcer disease

  • Posterior duodenal ulcer → gastroduodenal artery

  • UGI bleeding → haematemesis and/or melaena

  • Major causes → PUD, varices, erosive disease, malignancy

  • NSAIDs → important risk factor for ulcer bleeding

Exam Pearl: Upper GIT bleeding: think peptic ulcer disease first.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩১) Any age with large goiter, poor drug compliance & recurrent thyrotoxicosis demands......?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A patient with a large goiter, poor compliance with antithyroid medication, and recurrent thyrotoxicosis is best managed with a definitive treatment rather than repeated courses of medication. Radioiodine (I-131) therapy is a commonly used definitive treatment for Graves’ disease and is particularly appropriate when adherence to long-term antithyroid therapy is poor. However, an important caveat is that very large goiters, compressive symptoms, or suspected malignancy favor thyroidectomy because radioiodine may be less effective in very large glands and does not provide immediate decompression. Given the wording and available options, radioiodine is the intended answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Poor compliance + recurrent thyrotoxicosis → consider definitive therapy

  • Radioiodine → common definitive treatment for Graves’ disease

  • Large/compressive goiter → thyroidectomy may be preferred

  • Antithyroid drugs → useful for control but require adherence

  • Radioiodine usually results in eventual hypothyroidism, requiring levothyroxine

Exam Pearl: Recurrent thyrotoxicosis with poor drug compliance generally calls for definitive therapy; radioiodine is the classic exam answer unless a large/compressive goiter mandates surgery.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩২) Which is investigation of choice after 7 days of stroke?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
MRI of the brain is the best investigation among these options for detecting a cerebral infarction after the acute phase of stroke. Diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) is highly sensitive for acute ischemic infarction and can detect lesions much earlier than conventional CT. After about 7 days, the infarct is usually well established, and MRI provides excellent anatomical detail and can demonstrate the extent and location of the lesion. CT remains the initial investigation in suspected acute stroke because it is rapid and reliably excludes intracranial hemorrhage, but it is less sensitive for small or posterior fossa infarcts. MRA evaluates cerebral vessels rather than being the primary test for identifying the brain lesion itself. LP is not a routine investigation for stroke.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stroke after 7 days → MRI is preferred for established infarction

  • DWI MRI → highly sensitive for ischemic stroke

  • CT → first-line in acute suspected stroke, especially to exclude hemorrhage

  • MRA → evaluates cerebral vasculature

  • LP → not routine for uncomplicated stroke

Exam Pearl: MRI is more sensitive than CT for detecting cerebral infarction, especially small or posterior lesions.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৩) Panic disorder is often associated with.......?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Panic disorder is characterized by recurrent, unexpected panic attacks followed by persistent concern about additional attacks or maladaptive behavioral changes. It is commonly associated with agoraphobia, in which the person develops fear or avoidance of situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable if panic symptoms occur. Patients may therefore avoid public transport, crowds, open or enclosed spaces, or being outside alone. Stress can precipitate or worsen panic symptoms but is not the characteristic psychiatric association tested here. OCD is a separate anxiety-related disorder and may coexist with panic disorder, but it is not the classic association. “HCR” is not a standard major association of panic disorder.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Panic disorder → recurrent unexpected panic attacks

  • Common association → agoraphobia

  • Agoraphobia → fear/avoidance of situations where escape may be difficult

  • Panic attacks → sudden intense fear with autonomic symptoms

  • Panic disorder can coexist with depression and other anxiety disorders

Exam Pearl: Panic disorder is classically associated with agoraphobia.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৪) Which is most common source of hemorrhage in SAH?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The most common source of spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is rupture of an intracranial saccular (berry) aneurysm. Among the vessels listed, the anterior communicating artery (ACom) region is the most common site for these aneurysms. The ACom connects the two anterior cerebral arteries and is part of the circle of Willis, where congenital and hemodynamic factors predispose to aneurysm formation. Rupture produces blood in the subarachnoid space and classically presents with a sudden, severe “thunderclap headache,” often described as the worst headache of the patient's life. Posterior communicating artery aneurysms are also common and may cause third-nerve palsy, while MCA aneurysms can present with focal neurological deficits.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common cause of spontaneous SAH → ruptured berry aneurysm

  • Commonest aneurysm site → anterior communicating artery region

  • Classic presentation → sudden thunderclap headache

  • PCom aneurysm → may cause CN III palsy

  • Berry aneurysms → commonly occur at circle of Willis

Exam Pearl: SAH + berry aneurysm: remember the anterior communicating artery as the classic commonest site.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৫) Diagnostic criteria of anorexia nervosa excludes......?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Anorexia nervosa is characterized by restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, an intense fear of gaining weight, and persistent behaviors that prevent weight gain. Patients commonly avoid high-calorie foods and may use excessive exercise or other compensatory behaviors. In older diagnostic criteria, amenorrhoea was included as a typical feature, although it is no longer required in DSM-5. A historical examination criterion was weight loss of approximately 15% or more below expected body weight. Recurrent binge eating, however, is not a defining feature of anorexia nervosa; recurrent binge eating with compensatory behaviors is characteristic of the binge-eating/purging subtype of anorexia nervosa but is not required and may be absent. Therefore, among these options, recurrent bouts of binge eating is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anorexia nervosa → significantly low body weight

  • Intense fear of weight gain

  • Avoidance/restriction of high-calorie foods

  • Amenorrhoea → historical criterion; not required in DSM-5

  • Binge eating may occur in the binge-eating/purging subtype, but is not universal

Exam Pearl: Anorexia nervosa is fundamentally a disorder of restriction and low body weight; recurrent binge eating is not a required diagnostic feature.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৬) 'Patient believes that he is dead or part or organ of his body is dead, the world and even time has been lost or destroyed' - the patient is suffering from what type of delusion?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A nihilistic delusion is a false, fixed belief that the patient, their body, an organ, or aspects of the external world do not exist, are dead, or have been destroyed. The classic description includes believing that one is dead, that a body part has disappeared or is dead, or that the world, time, or existence itself has ceased. Nihilistic delusions are classically associated with severe depressive illness, particularly psychotic depression, and may occur in Cotard syndrome. Grandiose delusions involve exaggerated beliefs about power or importance, persecution delusions involve being harmed or persecuted, and hypochondriacal delusions concern having a serious illness.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nihilistic delusion → “I am dead” or “the world no longer exists”

  • Cotard syndrome → prominent nihilistic delusions

  • Common association → severe depression with psychotic features

  • Grandiose → exaggerated power, wealth, identity, or importance

  • Persecutory → belief of being harmed or persecuted

Exam Pearl: Belief that oneself, body parts, or the world is dead/nonexistent = nihilistic delusion (Cotard syndrome).

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৭) Which is a pathognomonic lesion of scabies?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A burrow is the characteristic and essentially pathognomonic lesion of scabies. It is a thin, short, wavy or thread-like track in the superficial epidermis produced by the female Sarcoptes scabiei mite as it tunnels through the stratum corneum and deposits eggs. Burrows are commonly found in the finger webs, flexor surfaces of the wrists, sides of the fingers, genital region, and around the waist. Papules and crusts can occur in scabies but are nonspecific. Comedones are characteristic of acne, not scabies. Therefore, the presence of a typical burrow strongly supports the diagnosis of scabies.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Scabies → burrow

  • Cause → Sarcoptes scabiei

  • Burrow location → stratum corneum

  • Common sites → finger webs, wrists, genitalia, waist

  • Severe pruritus, often worse at night

Exam Pearl: A burrow is the classic pathognomonic lesion of scabies.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৮) Gram negative diplococci in microscopy is suggestive of which disease?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the causative organism of gonorrhoea, is a Gram-negative diplococcus that characteristically appears as kidney-bean-shaped organisms, often found intracellularly within neutrophils in urethral discharge. This microscopic finding is particularly useful for diagnosing gonococcal urethritis in symptomatic men. Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum, a spirochete that is not reliably visualized by routine Gram staining. AIDS is caused by HIV, a virus, while chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, a Gram-negative coccobacillus. Therefore, the presence of Gram-negative diplococci strongly suggests gonorrhoea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gram-negative diplococcus → Neisseria gonorrhoeae

  • Gonococcus → often intracellular in neutrophils

  • Syphilis → Treponema pallidum

  • Chancroid → Haemophilus ducreyi

  • Gonorrhoea → commonly causes purulent urethral discharge

Exam Pearl: Intracellular Gram-negative diplococci in urethral pus = gonorrhoea.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৯) 'Cardiac enlargement due to hypertension' - what type of adaptive response is this?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cardiac enlargement due to chronic hypertension is an example of pathological hypertrophy. Hypertension increases afterload, particularly on the left ventricle, requiring cardiac myocytes to generate greater force to eject blood. Because adult cardiac myocytes have very limited proliferative capacity, the heart adapts primarily by increasing cell size, rather than cell number. This produces myocardial hypertrophy, initially helping maintain cardiac output but eventually potentially leading to diastolic dysfunction, myocardial ischemia, arrhythmias, and heart failure. It is considered pathological because it results from a chronic abnormal stimulus rather than a normal physiological demand. In contrast, physiological hypertrophy occurs with conditions such as regular exercise or pregnancy-related cardiovascular adaptation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypertension → increased afterload

  • Chronic pressure overload → left ventricular hypertrophy

  • Cardiac adaptation → mainly hypertrophy, not hyperplasia

  • Hypertension-induced cardiac enlargement → pathological hypertrophy

  • Exercise-related cardiac enlargement → physiological hypertrophy

Exam Pearl: Chronic hypertension causes pathological cardiac hypertrophy due to pressure overload.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪০) What type of metaplasia occurs in lung of smoker?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chronic exposure to cigarette smoke causes the normal ciliated pseudostratified columnar epithelium of the respiratory tract to undergo squamous metaplasia. In this adaptive process, the normal columnar epithelium is replaced by stratified squamous epithelium, which is more resistant to chronic irritation but loses important functions such as mucociliary clearance. Persistent smoking-related injury can cause further progression from metaplasia to dysplasia and eventually squamous cell carcinoma. This change is therefore considered a protective adaptation initially, but it increases susceptibility to malignant transformation if the damaging stimulus persists.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Smoking → squamous metaplasia in respiratory epithelium

  • Normal airway epithelium → ciliated pseudostratified columnar

  • Metaplastic epithelium → stratified squamous

  • Loss of cilia → impaired mucociliary clearance

  • Persistent injury → metaplasia → dysplasia → carcinoma

Exam Pearl: Smoker's lung: ciliated columnar epithelium undergoes squamous metaplasia.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪১) Which is not true about necrosis?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Necrosis is characterized by irreversible cell injury with loss of plasma membrane integrity. The damaged cell undergoes cellular swelling, organelle breakdown, and leakage of intracellular contents into the surrounding tissue. Characteristic nuclear changes include pyknosis, karyorrhexis, and karyolysis. Enzymatic digestion of cellular components by lysosomal enzymes is also an important feature of necrotic cell death. In contrast, an intact plasma membrane is not a feature of necrosis; membrane disruption and increased permeability are characteristic. This contrasts with apoptosis, where the plasma membrane generally remains intact and cellular fragments are packaged into apoptotic bodies.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Necrosis → loss of plasma membrane integrity

  • Cellular swelling → common early feature

  • Nuclear changes → pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis

  • Enzymatic digestion → characteristic of necrotic cell death

  • Apoptosis → plasma membrane remains intact

Exam Pearl: Necrosis = membrane rupture and leakage; an intact plasma membrane is not a feature.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪২) Nuclear changes following necrosis excludes.....?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The characteristic nuclear changes in necrosis are pyknosis, karyorrhexis, and karyolysis. Pyknosis refers to nuclear shrinkage with increased basophilia due to chromatin condensation. Karyorrhexis is fragmentation of the pyknotic nucleus, while karyolysis is dissolution or fading of the nucleus due to DNase-mediated degradation of DNA. Karyocytes is not a recognized nuclear change of necrosis; it generally refers to a nucleated cell rather than a specific pathological nuclear alteration. Therefore, karyocytes is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pyknosis → nuclear shrinkage and chromatin condensation

  • Karyorrhexis → nuclear fragmentation

  • Karyolysis → nuclear dissolution/fading

  • Sequence often remembered as Pyknosis → Karyorrhexis → Karyolysis

Exam Pearl: Necrotic nuclear changes = Pyknosis, Karyorrhexis, Karyolysis.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৩) Which enzyme does not take part in destruction of free radicals?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Catalase, superoxide dismutase (SOD), and glutathione peroxidase are major antioxidant enzymes that protect cells by neutralizing reactive oxygen species (ROS). SOD converts superoxide radicals (O₂⁻) into hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), while catalase and glutathione peroxidase then convert H₂O₂ into less harmful products, mainly water. Myeloperoxidase (MPO), in contrast, is primarily a microbicidal enzyme in neutrophils. It uses H₂O₂ and chloride ions to generate hypochlorous acid (HOCl), an important antimicrobial oxidant. Thus, rather than detoxifying free radicals, MPO contributes to their generation for microbial killing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • SOD → superoxide → H₂O₂

  • Catalase → H₂O₂ → H₂O + O₂

  • Glutathione peroxidase → H₂O₂/lipid peroxides → less harmful products

  • Myeloperoxidase → H₂O₂ + Cl⁻ → HOCl

  • MPO → important for neutrophil microbial killing

Exam Pearl: SOD, catalase, and glutathione peroxidase are antioxidant defenses; myeloperoxidase generates HOCl for microbial killing.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৪) Which is not a criteria of dry gangrene?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Dry gangrene results from loss of arterial blood supply, usually without significant bacterial infection. Because venous drainage remains relatively intact, the affected tissue becomes dry, shrunken, dark, and mummified. The process is typically slowly progressive, allowing a clear line of demarcation to develop between viable and non-viable tissue. Therefore, an absent line of demarcation is not a feature of dry gangrene. In contrast, wet gangrene involves infection, tissue swelling, putrefaction, and rapid spread, with a poorly defined or absent line of demarcation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Dry gangrene → arterial occlusion

  • Tissue → dry, shrunken, black, mummified

  • Spread → slow

  • Venous drainage → relatively preserved

  • Clear line of demarcation → characteristic

  • Wet gangrene → infection, oedema, rapid spread, poor demarcation

Exam Pearl: Dry gangrene is slowly progressive and has a clear line of demarcation.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৫) Oedema is clinically evident when there is an excess of fluid by---?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Oedema becomes clinically apparent when the interstitial fluid volume increases sufficiently to produce visible or palpable swelling. In standard pathology teaching, clinically detectable oedema is generally said to occur when there is approximately a 15% increase in interstitial fluid volume. Initially, the lymphatic system can compensate for increased interstitial fluid by increasing lymphatic drainage. Once this compensatory capacity is exceeded, fluid accumulates progressively in the interstitial space and becomes clinically evident as oedema. This is an important concept in understanding the early compensatory mechanisms of fluid balance and the development of tissue swelling.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Clinically evident oedema → approximately 15% excess fluid

  • Early increase in interstitial fluid → compensated by lymphatic drainage

  • Oedema → excess fluid in the interstitial tissue

  • Major mechanisms → increased hydrostatic pressure, reduced plasma oncotic pressure, lymphatic obstruction, sodium retention, inflammation

Exam Pearl: Clinical oedema becomes apparent at approximately 15% excess interstitial fluid.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৬) Which doesn’t happen by excessive formation of repair tissue?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Excessive formation of repair tissue can produce abnormal fibroblastic proliferation and excessive collagen deposition, resulting in conditions such as keloid and hypertrophic scar. Desmoid (likely what is meant by “Desmid”) is also a fibroblastic proliferative lesion associated with excessive connective-tissue growth. In contrast, wound dehiscence occurs because of inadequate wound healing or insufficient tensile strength, causing partial or complete separation of previously approximated wound edges. Risk factors include infection, poor nutrition, excessive tension, corticosteroid therapy, and impaired collagen synthesis. Therefore, wound dehiscence does not result from excessive formation of repair tissue.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Excessive repair → keloid

  • Excessive repair → hypertrophic scar

  • Desmoid → fibroblastic proliferation

  • Inadequate repair → wound dehiscence

  • Wound strength depends largely on collagen deposition and remodeling

Exam Pearl: Excessive repair causes scars/keloids; inadequate repair causes wound dehiscence.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৭) Which is not a common site for passive congestion?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Passive congestion (venous congestion) occurs when impaired venous outflow causes accumulation of blood within tissues. The lungs, liver, and spleen are classic organs affected by passive congestion. In left-sided heart failure, pulmonary venous congestion produces pulmonary oedema and, chronically, “brown induration” of the lungs. In right-sided heart failure, hepatic venous congestion produces a nutmeg liver, while chronic systemic venous congestion can also affect the spleen. A lymph node is not a typical or common site of passive blood congestion because its main function involves lymphatic drainage and immune surveillance rather than serving as a major venous blood reservoir. Therefore, the lymph node is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Passive congestion → impaired venous outflow

  • Lung → left-sided heart failure

  • Liver → right-sided heart failure

  • Spleen → chronic systemic venous congestion

  • Lymph node → not a common site

Exam Pearl: Classic organs of passive congestion: lungs, liver, and spleen; lymph nodes are not typical.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৮) Rhabdomyoma is a benign tumor of which tissue?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Rhabdomyoma is a benign tumor showing differentiation toward striated skeletal muscle. It is rare and occurs in two main forms: adult rhabdomyoma, which commonly arises in the head and neck region, and fetal rhabdomyoma, which occurs predominantly in the head and neck of children. Cardiac rhabdomyoma is a separate, distinctive benign tumor of cardiac muscle and is strongly associated with tuberous sclerosis, particularly in children. Despite the similar name, cardiac rhabdomyoma is not classified as the typical rhabdomyoma of skeletal muscle. Leiomyoma is the benign tumor of smooth muscle, while lipoma arises from adipose tissue.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rhabdomyoma → skeletal muscle differentiation

  • Leiomyoma → smooth muscle

  • Lipoma → fat

  • Cardiac rhabdomyoma → associated with tuberous sclerosis

  • Adult rhabdomyoma → commonly head and neck

Exam Pearl: Rhabdomyoma = benign skeletal muscle tumor; rhabdomyoma of the heart is a distinct cardiac tumor.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৯) Which is not criteria of benign tumor?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pleomorphism means marked variation in the size and shape of cells and their nuclei. It is a characteristic feature of malignant tumors, reflecting cellular atypia and loss of normal differentiation. In contrast, benign tumors are generally well differentiated, resemble the tissue of origin, grow relatively slowly, and typically do not metastasize. Although some benign tumors can show mild variation in cell size or shape, significant pleomorphism is not a defining criterion of benignity. Therefore, among the given options, pleomorphism present is the feature that is not characteristic of a benign tumor.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Benign tumor → well differentiated

  • Benign tumor → usually slow growing

  • Benign tumor → no metastasis

  • Malignant tumor → pleomorphism, atypia, abnormal mitoses

  • Pleomorphism = variation in cellular and nuclear size/shape

Exam Pearl: Pleomorphism strongly suggests malignancy, whereas benign tumors are typically well differentiated and non-metastatic.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫০) Which one is tumor marker for breast cancer?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
CA 15-3 is the tumor marker most classically associated with breast cancer. It is a circulating mucin-associated antigen derived from the MUC1 glycoprotein. Its main clinical use is monitoring response to treatment and detecting recurrence or progression, particularly in advanced or metastatic breast cancer. It is not sufficiently sensitive or specific for screening or diagnosis of breast cancer. CA-125 is mainly associated with ovarian cancer, while CA 19-9 is primarily associated with pancreatic and biliary tract malignancies. CEA may also be elevated in breast cancer and can be used in some settings for monitoring, but CA 15-3 is the classic exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Breast cancer → CA 15-3

  • Ovarian cancer → CA-125

  • Pancreatic cancer → CA 19-9

  • Colorectal cancer → CEA

  • CA 15-3 → mainly useful for monitoring, not screening

Exam Pearl: Breast cancer tumor marker: CA 15-3.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫১) Which is the event of 3rd phase of response after acute hemorrhage?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
After acute hemorrhage, the body's compensatory response occurs in phases. Initially, there is a rapid neurogenic response with peripheral vasoconstriction to maintain blood pressure and perfusion of vital organs. Subsequently, hormonal mechanisms become important. In the later phase, reduced renal perfusion activates the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) and increases ADH secretion, leading to renal sodium and water retention and restoration of circulating volume. Reticulocytosis occurs later as the bone marrow responds to blood loss, generally over several days, rather than being an immediate third-phase response. Therefore, fluid retention by the kidney is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute hemorrhage → vasoconstriction initially

  • RAAS activation → Na⁺ and water retention

  • ADH → increased water reabsorption

  • Reticulocytosis → delayed marrow response to blood loss

  • Goal of compensation → restore circulating blood volume

Exam Pearl: Late compensation after hemorrhage involves renal sodium and water retention.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫২) All of the tissues are particularly sensitive to ionizing radiation except.......?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Tissues differ in their sensitivity to ionizing radiation, largely according to their rate of cell division and degree of cellular differentiation. Bone marrow and gonads are highly radiosensitive because they contain rapidly dividing cells. The skin is also relatively radiosensitive, with radiation exposure potentially causing erythema, epilation, and other tissue injury. The thyroid is comparatively less radiosensitive to direct radiation injury than these tissues, although it is clinically important because radiation exposure, particularly in childhood, increases the risk of thyroid carcinoma. Therefore, among the given options, the thyroid is the best answer as the tissue that is relatively less radiosensitive.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Highly radiosensitive → bone marrow

  • Highly radiosensitive → gonads

  • Skin → relatively radiosensitive

  • Thyroid → relatively less radiosensitive to direct tissue injury

  • Rapidly dividing, poorly differentiated cells → generally more radiosensitive

Exam Pearl: Bone marrow and gonads are highly radiosensitive; thyroid is the exception among these options.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৩) VDRL test is positive in...% case of secondary syphilis?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) test is a non-treponemal test for syphilis. Its sensitivity is highest during secondary syphilis, when there is a high circulating antibody (reagin) titre. Standard examination figures commonly quote VDRL as positive in approximately 95% of patients with secondary syphilis. However, sensitivity is not 100%, and occasional false-negative results can occur, including because of the prozone phenomenon in patients with very high antibody titres. Treponemal tests such as TPHA or FTA-ABS are more specific and are used to confirm infection.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • VDRL → non-treponemal test

  • Highest sensitivity → secondary syphilis

  • Secondary syphilis → VDRL approximately 95% positive

  • False-positive VDRL → possible

  • Prozone phenomenon → can cause a false-negative result

Exam Pearl: VDRL is positive in about 95% of secondary syphilis cases.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৪) Which one is diagnostic criteria of severe malaria according to national guideline?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Severe malaria is diagnosed when a patient with Plasmodium falciparum infection develops one or more established severe manifestations. Repeated generalized convulsions—classically more than two episodes within 24 hours—are a recognized criterion for severe malaria and indicate cerebral involvement. The other options are not correct as stated. Hematocrit >15% does not define severe malaria; severe malarial anaemia is associated with a markedly reduced haemoglobin/haematocrit, not an elevated value. Similarly, urine output <400 mL/24 hours is not the standard national criterion for oliguria in severe malaria; severe renal impairment is assessed using established clinical and biochemical criteria.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Severe malaria → usually due to P. falciparum

  • Repeated convulsions → >2 episodes/24 h

  • Cerebral malaria → impaired consciousness/coma

  • Severe anaemia → markedly low Hb/haematocrit

  • Acute kidney injury → rising creatinine and/or significant oliguria

Exam Pearl: Repeated generalized convulsions (>2 in 24 hours) are a recognized severe-malaria criterion.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৫) Which one is contraindicated in a patient of uncomplicated gonorrhoea with pregnancy?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone, is contraindicated in pregnancy because fluoroquinolones are generally avoided during pregnancy due to concerns regarding effects on developing cartilage and musculoskeletal tissue. For uncomplicated gonorrhoea in pregnancy, ceftriaxone is the preferred treatment. Cefixime is an alternative oral cephalosporin when ceftriaxone cannot be used. Spectinomycin has historically been used as an alternative in pregnancy and is not associated with the same fetal cartilage concern as fluoroquinolones. Therefore, among the given options, ofloxacin is the contraindicated drug.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pregnancy + gonorrhoea → ceftriaxone preferred

  • Fluoroquinolones → avoid/contraindicated in pregnancy

  • Ofloxacin → fluoroquinolone

  • Cefixime → alternative cephalosporin

  • Gonorrhoea → caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae

Exam Pearl: Pregnant patient with gonorrhoea: use a cephalosporin such as ceftriaxone; avoid ofloxacin.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৬) Normal myeloid/ erythroid ratio is---?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The normal myeloid-to-erythroid (M:E) ratio in adult bone marrow is approximately 3:1, meaning myeloid precursors are normally about three times as numerous as erythroid precursors. This ratio reflects the relative production of granulocytic and erythroid cells in the bone marrow. An increased M:E ratio may occur when myeloid production is increased or erythroid production is suppressed, while a decreased M:E ratio can occur with increased erythropoiesis or reduced granulopoiesis. The normal range is approximately 2:1 to 4:1, making 3:1 the standard exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Normal M:E ratio → 3:1

  • Normal range → approximately 2:1–4:1

  • Increased M:E → myeloid hyperplasia or erythroid suppression

  • Decreased M:E → erythroid hyperplasia or myeloid suppression

  • Assessed in bone marrow examination

Exam Pearl: Normal myeloid : erythroid ratio = 3 : 1.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৭) What is not the evidence of red cell damage?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fragmented red cells (schistocytes), Heinz bodies, and spherocytes are all morphological findings that can indicate red-cell damage or destruction. Schistocytes result from mechanical fragmentation of erythrocytes, as seen in microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. Heinz bodies represent denatured hemoglobin, typically due to oxidative damage, as in G6PD deficiency. Spherocytes are associated with membrane loss and extravascular hemolysis, classically in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Howell-Jolly bodies, however, are nuclear DNA remnants within erythrocytes and primarily indicate absent or reduced splenic function, such as after splenectomy or in functional asplenia. Thus, they are not evidence of red-cell damage per se.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Schistocytes → mechanical RBC fragmentation

  • Heinz bodies → oxidized/denatured Hb

  • Spherocytes → membrane loss, extravascular hemolysis

  • Howell-Jolly bodies → absent/hypofunctional spleen

  • Howell-Jolly bodies are nuclear remnants

Exam Pearl: Howell-Jolly bodies indicate splenic dysfunction, not primary red-cell damage.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৮) What is not true about non hodgkin’s lymphoma?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: Single axial group of lymph node is usually involved
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) typically shows non-contiguous (“skip”) spread, unlike the more predictable contiguous spread classically seen in Hodgkin lymphoma. Extranodal involvement is common in NHL and may involve sites such as the gastrointestinal tract, skin, bone marrow, or CNS. Histologically, NHL usually demonstrates a monomorphic population of malignant lymphoid cells, reflecting clonal proliferation. In contrast, involvement of a single axial group of lymph nodes is not characteristic; NHL often involves multiple, non-contiguous nodal groups and/or extranodal sites. Therefore, option B is the statement that is not true.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • NHL → non-contiguous spread

  • Extranodal disease → common

  • Histology → usually monomorphic

  • Hodgkin lymphoma → classically contiguous nodal spread

  • NHL can involve multiple nodal and extranodal sites

Exam Pearl: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma characteristically spreads non-contiguously and commonly involves extranodal sites.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৯) Which of the following is automated method for hemoglobin estimation?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cell counter method is the automated method for hemoglobin estimation. Modern automated hematology analyzers (cell counters) measure hemoglobin after lysing red blood cells and photometrically determining the released hemoglobin, providing rapid and standardized results. The acid hematin method (Sahli’s method) is a manual colorimetric technique and is less accurate. The oxyhemoglobin method is also a manual spectrophotometric method. The cyanmethemoglobin (Drabkin’s) method is a standard reference laboratory method but is generally performed manually or semi-automatically rather than being the characteristic automated method referred to in this MCQ. Therefore, cell counter method is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Automated Hb estimation → cell counter/hematology analyzer

  • Sahli’s method → acid hematin, manual

  • Cyanmethemoglobin → reference method, manual/semi-automated

  • Automated analyzers → rapid, precise, and reproducible

Exam Pearl: For automated hemoglobin estimation, think automated hematology analyzer (cell counter).

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬০) Bacterial spores are destroyed by following process excludes...?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pasteurization does not reliably destroy bacterial spores because it uses relatively low temperatures for a limited period and is designed primarily to reduce vegetative pathogenic microorganisms rather than achieve sterilization. In contrast, autoclaving uses saturated steam under pressure and reliably destroys bacterial spores. A hot-air oven achieves sterilization through dry heat and can destroy spores when appropriate temperature and exposure times are used. Gamma radiation is an effective sterilizing method that can destroy bacterial spores by causing DNA damage. Therefore, pasteurization is the process that does not reliably destroy bacterial spores.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Autoclaving → destroys spores

  • Hot-air oven → destroys spores

  • Gamma radiation → destroys spores

  • Pasteurization → mainly reduces vegetative bacteria

  • Pasteurization ≠ sterilization

Exam Pearl: Pasteurization is not a sterilization method and does not reliably destroy bacterial spores.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬১) ‘Filariform larva’ is the infective form of which worm?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The filariform larva (third-stage, L3 larva) is the infective stage of hookworms, particularly Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus. These larvae develop in soil from rhabditiform larvae and are capable of penetrating intact human skin, commonly through bare feet. After penetration, they enter the circulation, migrate through the lungs, ascend the trachea, are swallowed, and finally mature into adult worms in the small intestine. In contrast, pinworm is acquired by ingestion of embryonated eggs, while Ascaris lumbricoides is acquired by ingestion of embryonated eggs containing larvae. Tapeworms have different infective stages depending on the species.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hookworm infective stage → Filariform (L3) larva

  • Route → skin penetration

  • Hookworms → Ancylostoma duodenale, Necator americanus

  • Diagnostic stage → Rhabditiform eggs/larvae in stool depending on species/testing context

  • Hookworm migration → skin → blood → lungs → intestine

Exam Pearl: Filariform L3 larva = infective stage of hookworm.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬২) Which one is the most common Causes of cirrhosis of liver in our country?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In Bangladesh, chronic viral hepatitis, particularly hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, has historically been a major cause of liver cirrhosis. Persistent viral infection causes chronic hepatic inflammation and repeated hepatocyte injury, leading to progressive fibrosis, regenerative nodule formation, and ultimately cirrhosis. Alcohol-related cirrhosis is less dominant in Bangladesh compared with many Western populations. NAFLD/NASH is an increasingly important cause of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis, particularly with rising metabolic risk factors, but for traditional examination questions asking the commonest cause “in our country,” chronic viral hepatitis is the accepted answer. Primary sclerosing cholangitis is a much less common cause.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bangladesh → historically major cirrhosis cause: chronic viral hepatitis

  • Important viruses → HBV and HCV

  • Chronic injury → inflammation → fibrosis → cirrhosis

  • NAFLD/NASH → increasingly important

  • Alcohol → less prominent than in many Western populations

Exam Pearl: For traditional Bangladesh-based exams: chronic viral hepatitis is the best answer for the commonest cause of cirrhosis.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৩) Which is not true about staphylococcus?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci that characteristically appear in grape-like clusters on microscopy. All clinically important Staphylococcus species are catalase positive, which helps differentiate them from Streptococcus and Enterococcus species, which are catalase negative. However, not all Staphylococcus species are coagulase positive. Staphylococcus aureus is typically coagulase positive, whereas common coagulase-negative staphylococci such as S. epidermidis and S. saprophyticus are coagulase negative. Therefore, the statement that all staphylococci are coagulase positive is false.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Staphylococcus → Gram-positive cocci

  • Arrangement → grape-like clusters

  • Staphylococci → catalase positive

  • S. aureus → coagulase positive

  • S. epidermidis, S. saprophyticus → coagulase negative

Exam Pearl: All staphylococci are catalase positive, but only some—classically S. aureus—are coagulase positive.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৪) Which one is not correct regarding trismus in tetanus?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Explanation:
Trismus (lockjaw) is an early and characteristic manifestation of tetanus caused by the action of tetanospasmin, which blocks inhibitory neurotransmitter release in the CNS, producing sustained muscle rigidity and spasms. Involvement of the masseter muscles causes difficulty opening the mouth, hence the term “lockjaw.” Patients may also have difficulty masticating and swallowing because of persistent muscle spasm. Although tetanic spasms can be extremely painful, pain is not a defining feature of trismus itself and is not usually included as a characteristic clinical criterion. Therefore, among the given options, “very painful condition” is the best answer for the statement that is not correct.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tetanus → trismus (lockjaw)

  • Main muscle involved → masseter

  • Mechanism → loss of inhibitory neurotransmission

  • Tetanospasmin blocks GABA and glycine release

  • Other features → risus sardonicus, opisthotonus, muscle rigidity

Exam Pearl: Trismus in tetanus = masseter spasm causing inability to open the mouth.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৫) Which drug is used for the elimination of luminal cyst in amoebic dysentry?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Diloxanide furoate is a luminal amoebicide used to eradicate Entamoeba histolytica organisms, particularly cysts, remaining in the intestinal lumen after treatment of invasive amoebiasis. In amoebic dysentery, metronidazole or tinidazole is used primarily to treat the tissue-invasive trophozoites. Because these tissue agents do not reliably eradicate luminal infection, a luminal agent such as diloxanide furoate is subsequently given to eliminate residual organisms and reduce relapse and transmission. Nitazoxanide is not the standard first-line luminal amoebicide for this purpose.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Amoebic dysentery → Entamoeba histolytica

  • Tissue amoebicide → Metronidazole / Tinidazole

  • Luminal amoebicide → Diloxanide furoate

  • Luminal treatment helps eliminate residual cysts/organisms

  • Treating invasive disease alone may lead to persistent carriage/relapse

Exam Pearl: Amoebic dysentery: metronidazole for tissue invasion, followed by diloxanide furoate for luminal eradication.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৬) Tuberculosis cannot affect the following except....?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The wording is ambiguous: “cannot affect ... except” means which site can be affected by tuberculosis. The lung is by far the most common site of TB and is the primary site of infection in most patients. TB can also rarely involve the thyroid, pancreas, and myocardium, but these are uncommon extrapulmonary sites. Pulmonary TB occurs after inhalation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with infection primarily involving the alveoli and regional lymph nodes. Therefore, among the options, the lung is the clear and most accepted answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common site of TB → Lung

  • Extrapulmonary TB → lymph nodes, pleura, bone, meninges, kidney, etc.

  • Thyroid, pancreas, myocardium → rare sites

  • Pulmonary TB is the major source of transmission

Exam Pearl: TB can involve almost any organ, but the lung is its most common site.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৭) Which is not true about ulcerative colitis?
