Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that is limited to the colon and rectum, so it does not occur throughout the gastrointestinal tract. It typically begins in the rectum and extends proximally in a continuous pattern. Inflammation is predominantly confined to the mucosa and submucosa, producing superficial ulceration. Granulomas are characteristically absent, helping distinguish UC from Crohn disease. Long-standing extensive UC is associated with an increased risk of colorectal carcinoma, particularly with greater disease duration and extent. Therefore, “occurs throughout GIT” is the statement that is not true.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • UC → colon and rectum only

  • Distribution → continuous

  • Rectum → usually involved

  • Ulcers → superficial

  • Granulomas → absent

  • Long-standing extensive UC → increased colorectal cancer risk

Exam Pearl: UC is a continuous superficial colitis confined to the colon; Crohn disease can affect the entire GIT.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৮) Which of the following serves to cushion and insulate the skin and other organs?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Adipocytes are specialized connective-tissue cells that store triglycerides as fat. Adipose tissue provides important mechanical cushioning and insulation for the skin and internal organs. It also serves as an energy reserve and contributes to endocrine regulation through adipokines. Fibroblasts primarily synthesize extracellular matrix components such as collagen and elastin. Histiocytes/macrophages are involved mainly in phagocytosis and immune defense. Therefore, among the given options, the adipocyte is the cell responsible for the cushioning and insulating functions of adipose tissue.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adipocyte → fat storage, cushioning, insulation

  • Fibroblast → collagen and extracellular matrix synthesis

  • Macrophage → phagocytosis

  • Adipose tissue → important energy reservoir

  • Adipose tissue also has endocrine functions

Exam Pearl: Adipocytes provide mechanical cushioning and thermal insulation.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৯) Reticular connective tissue is absent in.....?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Reticular connective tissue forms a supportive framework, or stroma, for many lymphoid and hematopoietic organs. It is prominent in the bone marrow, liver, and many lymphoid organs. In the thymus, however, the supporting stroma is formed primarily by epithelial reticular cells, rather than typical reticular connective tissue fibers. Therefore, this question is somewhat ambiguous depending on whether it asks about reticular fibers or reticular connective tissue. Among the given options, pancreas is generally considered the best exam answer because it does not have a characteristic reticular connective-tissue stroma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Reticular fibers → mainly type III collagen

  • Bone marrow → reticular stroma

  • Liver → reticular framework

  • Thymus → epithelial reticular cells form the stroma

  • Pancreas → mainly collagenous connective tissue supporting framework

Exam Pearl: Thymus is the classic exception: its stroma is formed by epithelial reticular cells, not typical reticular connective tissue.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭০) Which of the following is not dense regular connective tissue?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Dense regular connective tissue contains densely packed, parallel collagen fibers arranged to withstand tensile forces mainly in one direction. Classic examples include tendons, most ligaments, and aponeuroses. In contrast, the dermis of the skin is predominantly composed of dense irregular connective tissue, in which collagen fibers are arranged in multiple directions. This arrangement allows the skin to resist mechanical stresses from different directions. Therefore, the dermis is not dense regular connective tissue.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Dense regular CT → parallel collagen fibers

  • Tendons → dense regular CT

  • Ligaments → dense regular CT

  • Aponeuroses → dense regular CT

  • Dermis → dense irregular CT

Exam Pearl: Tendons, ligaments, and aponeuroses are dense regular; dermis is dense irregular connective tissue.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭১) What is the content of lacunae?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Lacunae are small spaces within the mineralized matrix of bone that house mature bone cells called osteocytes. Osteocytes are former osteoblasts that become surrounded by the bone matrix they produced and reside within lacunae. Each osteocyte extends cytoplasmic processes through tiny channels called canaliculi, allowing communication with neighboring osteocytes and exchange of nutrients and waste products. Osteoblasts are located mainly on bone surfaces where they synthesize new bone matrix, while osteoclasts are large multinucleated cells found in resorption cavities called Howship lacunae. Osteoprogenitor cells are stem/progenitor cells that give rise to osteoblasts.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bone lacuna → osteocyte

  • Canaliculi → contain osteocyte processes

  • Osteoblast → bone-forming cell on bone surface

  • Osteoclast → bone-resorbing cell

  • Howship lacuna → resorption cavity containing osteoclast

Exam Pearl: Lacunae contain osteocytes; canaliculi contain their cytoplasmic processes.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭২) Which is the thickest histological layer of heart?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The myocardium is the thickest histological layer of the heart wall. It is composed predominantly of cardiac muscle tissue and is responsible for generating the force required for contraction and pumping blood. Its thickness varies between chambers: the left ventricular myocardium is the thickest because it must generate sufficient pressure to drive blood through the systemic circulation. The endocardium is the innermost layer and consists mainly of endothelium with underlying connective tissue. The epicardium is the outer layer, corresponding to the visceral layer of the serous pericardium. The subendothelial layer is part of the endocardium and is not the thickest layer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Heart wall → endocardium, myocardium, epicardium

  • Thickest layer → myocardium

  • Thickest myocardium → left ventricle

  • Myocardium → cardiac muscle

  • Endocardium → endothelial lining

Exam Pearl: Myocardium is the thickest layer of the heart wall, especially in the left ventricle.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) What is the location of conducting system of heart?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The conducting system of the heart consists of the sinoatrial (SA) node, atrioventricular (AV) node, AV bundle (bundle of His), bundle branches, and Purkinje fibers. The Purkinje fibers, which distribute the electrical impulse throughout the ventricular myocardium, are located mainly in the subendocardial layer of the ventricles. The SA and AV nodes are specialized cardiac muscle tissue located within the myocardium, but when the question asks for the histological location of the ventricular conducting system, the accepted exam answer is subendocardial layer. Purkinje fibers are larger, pale-staining cells containing abundant glycogen and relatively few myofibrils.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • SA node → pacemaker

  • AV node → delays conduction

  • Bundle of His → conducts to ventricles

  • Purkinje fibers → subendocardial layer

  • Purkinje fibers → rapid ventricular conduction

Exam Pearl: Purkinje fibers are located in the subendocardial layer of the ventricles.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৪) Which one collects blood from venules?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Small veins (venules) collect blood from capillary beds and then drain it into progressively larger veins. The smallest venules, called postcapillary venules, receive blood directly from capillaries and are important sites for leukocyte migration and fluid exchange. Blood then passes from small veins into medium-sized veins, followed by large veins, which ultimately return blood to the heart. Capillaries connect arterioles to venules and therefore do not collect blood from venules. Thus, among the options, the small vein is the best answer for the vessel that receives blood from venules.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Capillaries → drain into venules

  • Venules → drain into small veins

  • Small veins → medium veins → large veins

  • Postcapillary venules → major site of leukocyte extravasation

Exam Pearl: Blood flows from capillaries → venules → small veins → medium veins → large veins.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৫) Which is the most prominent feature of elastic arteries?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).option4: Adventitia is much thinner than the media
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The most prominent histological feature of elastic arteries is their very thick tunica media, which contains numerous layers of fenestrated elastic lamellae interspersed with smooth muscle cells. This structure allows elastic arteries such as the aorta to expand during ventricular systole and recoil during diastole, thereby maintaining continuous blood flow. Elastic arteries do have vasa vasorum, particularly because their walls are too thick to be nourished adequately by diffusion from the lumen. The tunica intima is relatively well developed, but the dominant distinguishing feature is the elastic-rich tunica media. The adventitia is thinner than the media but contains important vasa vasorum and nerves.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Elastic arteries → thick tunica media

  • Media → numerous elastic lamellae

  • Function → Windkessel effect

  • Examples → aorta, pulmonary trunk

  • Vasa vasorum → present

Exam Pearl: Elastic artery = thick, elastic-rich tunica media.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৬) Which is a superficial reflex?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The plantar reflex is a classic superficial (cutaneous) reflex. It is elicited by stroking the lateral aspect of the sole of the foot, normally producing flexion of the toes. Its afferent limb travels through the tibial nerve and the response involves multiple spinal segments, mainly L5–S1. In contrast, the ankle jerk is a deep tendon reflex mediated mainly by S1, while the radial periosteal reflex is also a deep tendon/periosteal reflex. The finger flexion reflex is generally classified among deep reflexes rather than the standard superficial cutaneous reflexes. Therefore, the plantar reflex is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Superficial reflex → Plantar reflex

  • Plantar reflex → mainly L5–S1

  • Deep reflex → ankle jerk → S1

  • Deep reflex → radial periosteal reflex → C5–C6

  • Extensor plantar response (Babinski) → suggests UMN lesion

Exam Pearl: Plantar reflex is a superficial cutaneous reflex; ankle jerk is a deep tendon reflex.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৭) Endolymph has large quantity of ....... ?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Endolymph is the fluid within the membranous labyrinth of the inner ear and is characterized by a high potassium (K⁺) concentration and low sodium (Na⁺) concentration. This ionic composition is unusual compared with most extracellular fluids and is essential for normal auditory and vestibular transduction. The high K⁺ concentration contributes to the positive endocochlear potential, allowing K⁺ to enter sensory hair cells when mechanically gated channels open during sound or head movement. In contrast, perilymph has a composition more similar to extracellular fluid, with relatively high Na⁺ and low K⁺.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Endolymph → high K⁺, low Na⁺

  • Perilymph → high Na⁺, low K⁺

  • Endolymph → membranous labyrinth

  • Perilymph → bony labyrinth around membranous labyrinth

  • High K⁺ is essential for hair-cell transduction

Exam Pearl: Endolymph is potassium-rich; perilymph is sodium-rich.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৮) What is the root value of plantar response?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The plantar reflex is a superficial cutaneous reflex primarily mediated by the L5–S1 spinal segments, with contributions extending to S2. The afferent limb travels mainly through the tibial nerve, and the normal response is flexion of the toes. Clinically, the plantar response is particularly useful for assessing corticospinal tract (upper motor neuron) function. An extensor plantar response (Babinski sign) suggests an upper motor neuron lesion. Among the given options, L5 to S2 is the best accepted exam answer. The other options either extend too far rostrally or include sacral segments that are not the principal roots involved.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Plantar reflex → L5–S2

  • Most important roots → L5–S1

  • Nerve → tibial nerve

  • Normal response → flexion of toes

  • Babinski response → UMN/corticospinal tract lesion

Exam Pearl: Plantar reflex root value = L5–S2; remember L5–S1 as the principal levels.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৯) Which of the following degrades denatured or otherwise nonfunctional polypeptides?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Proteasomes are intracellular protein-degrading complexes that selectively break down denatured, damaged, misfolded, or otherwise nonfunctional proteins. Proteins destined for degradation are commonly tagged with ubiquitin and then delivered to the 26S proteasome, where they are degraded into smaller peptides. This ubiquitin–proteasome system is particularly important for regulating short-lived and abnormal intracellular proteins. Ribosomes synthesize proteins rather than degrade them. Lysosomes digest extracellular material taken up by endocytosis and various intracellular components through autophagy, while peroxisomes primarily carry out oxidative reactions, including fatty-acid metabolism and hydrogen peroxide detoxification.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Proteasome → degradation of ubiquitinated intracellular proteins

  • Ubiquitin → targets proteins for proteasomal degradation

  • Ribosome → protein synthesis

  • Lysosome → intracellular digestion/autophagy

  • Peroxisome → oxidation and H₂O₂ metabolism

Exam Pearl: Ubiquitin-tagged damaged or nonfunctional proteins → proteasome.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮০) Which is the longest part of cell cycle?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the phases listed, G1 phase is generally considered the longest phase of the actively dividing cell cycle. During G1, the cell grows, synthesizes RNA and proteins, produces organelles, and prepares for DNA replication in the S phase. The S phase is devoted mainly to DNA replication, while G2 involves further growth and preparation for mitosis and is usually shorter than G1. G0 is a quiescent state outside the active cell cycle and can vary greatly in duration; some cells remain in G0 for years or permanently. Therefore, when the question asks for the longest phase of the normal cell cycle among the given options, G1 is the accepted answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • G1 → cell growth and preparation for DNA synthesis

  • S → DNA replication

  • G2 → preparation for mitosis

  • M → mitosis and cytokinesis

  • G0 → quiescent/non-dividing state

Exam Pearl: G1 is the longest phase of the actively dividing cell cycle.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮১) In which phase of meiosis-1 bivalent occurs?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
During prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair with each other through a process called synapsis. This pairing begins during the zygotene stage and produces paired homologous chromosomes called bivalents (or tetrads, because each bivalent contains four chromatids). In leptotene, chromosomes begin to condense but homologous chromosomes have not yet fully paired. During pachytene, synapsis is complete and crossing over occurs. During diplotene, homologous chromosomes begin to separate but remain attached at chiasmata. Therefore, the formation of the bivalent is classically associated with the zygotene stage.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Leptotene → chromosome condensation

  • Zygotene → synapsis and bivalent formation

  • Pachytene → crossing over

  • Diplotene → chiasmata become visible

  • Diakinesis → terminalization of chiasmata

Exam Pearl: Zygotene = synapsis = bivalent formation.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮২) Which is not true about cornea?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).option1: Comprises anterior one-sixth of the eye
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The cornea is avascular, which is essential for maintaining its transparency and allowing light to pass through with minimal scattering. It receives nutrients mainly by diffusion from the tear film, aqueous humor, and peripheral blood vessels at the limbus. The cornea forms approximately the anterior one-sixth of the fibrous coat of the eyeball and is transparent. Classically, it is described as having five layers: epithelium, Bowman's membrane, stroma, Descemet's membrane, and endothelium. Therefore, the statement that the cornea is “completely vascular” is clearly incorrect.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cornea → avascular

  • Cornea → transparent

  • Anterior 1/6 of fibrous coat

  • Classical layers → 5

  • Nutrition → tears + aqueous humor + limbal vessels

Exam Pearl: Cornea is avascular; its transparency depends on its specialized structure and absence of blood vessels.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৩) Which is Antigen-presenting cells (APCs) in skin?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Langerhans cells are the principal antigen-presenting cells (APCs) of the epidermis. They are specialized dendritic cells located predominantly in the stratum spinosum. They capture and process antigens that enter the skin and then migrate to regional lymph nodes, where they present antigen-derived peptides to T lymphocytes via MHC class II molecules. Keratinocytes form the epidermal barrier and participate in innate immune signaling but are not the principal professional APCs. Merkel cells are associated with touch sensation, while melanocytes produce melanin and provide photoprotection. Therefore, Langerhans cells are the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Epidermal APC → Langerhans cell

  • Location → mainly stratum spinosum

  • Cell type → dendritic cell

  • Antigen presentation → MHC class II

  • Merkel cell → tactile sensation

  • Melanocyte → melanin production

Exam Pearl: Langerhans cells are the professional antigen-presenting cells of the epidermis.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৪) What is another name for the stratum germinativum?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Stratum germinativum is another name for the stratum basale, the deepest layer of the epidermis. It consists primarily of a single layer of cuboidal to columnar basal keratinocytes resting on the basement membrane. These cells undergo continuous mitosis and generate new keratinocytes that migrate upward through the epidermal layers. The stratum basale also contains melanocytes and Merkel cells. The stratum spinosum lies immediately above it, while the stratum lucidum is present only in thick skin and the stratum corneum is the superficial layer composed mainly of dead, keratinized cells.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stratum germinativum = stratum basale

  • Deepest epidermal layer

  • Main function → continuous cell renewal

  • Contains → basal keratinocytes, melanocytes, Merkel cells

  • Mitosis occurs mainly in stratum basale

Exam Pearl: Germinativum = Basale = deepest epidermal layer and the main site of keratinocyte proliferation.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৫) Which is not one of the specific layers of skin?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The skin proper consists of two principal layers: the epidermis and the dermis. The dermis is further divided into the papillary layer and reticular layer. The subcutaneous layer (hypodermis) lies beneath the skin and is composed mainly of loose connective tissue and adipose tissue; it is not considered a specific layer of the skin itself. Therefore, among the given options, subcutaneous layer is the best answer. The hypodermis is important for insulation, energy storage, and anchoring the skin to underlying structures.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Skin proper → epidermis + dermis

  • Dermis → papillary + reticular layers

  • Hypodermis → subcutaneous tissue, below skin

  • Hypodermis → mainly adipose + loose connective tissue

Exam Pearl: The skin consists of epidermis and dermis; the subcutaneous tissue lies beneath the skin.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৬) What is the dermatome of umbilicus?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The umbilicus corresponds to the T10 dermatome and is a classic anatomical landmark used in neurological examination. Dermatomes represent areas of skin supplied predominantly by sensory fibers from a single spinal nerve root. The T10 dermatome is centered around the umbilicus, while T4 corresponds to the nipple line and T6 to the xiphisternum. T12 is associated with the suprapubic region, and L1 is around the inguinal region. Therefore, the umbilicus is best remembered as T10.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nipple → T4

  • Xiphisternum → T6

  • Umbilicus → T10

  • Inguinal region → L1

  • Medial malleolus → L4

Exam Pearl: Umbilicus = T10.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৭) What is the Sensory Receptor of cochlea?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The spiral organ (organ of Corti) is the principal sensory receptor of the cochlea and is responsible for hearing. It is located on the basilar membrane within the cochlear duct and contains inner and outer hair cells. Sound-induced vibrations of the basilar membrane cause movement of the hair-cell stereocilia against the tectorial membrane, producing receptor potentials that are transmitted through the cochlear division of the vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII). Maculae are sensory receptors for linear acceleration and head position, while cristae ampullares detect angular acceleration in the semicircular ducts. Therefore, the spiral organ is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cochlear receptor → Organ of Corti (spiral organ)

  • Function → hearing

  • Location → basilar membrane

  • Vestibular receptor → maculae

  • Angular acceleration → crista ampullaris

Exam Pearl: Organ of Corti = sensory receptor for hearing.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৮) Which is true end artery?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The central retinal artery is a classic example of a true end artery. It supplies the inner layers of the retina and has essentially no significant anastomosis with neighboring arterial branches. Therefore, occlusion of the central retinal artery can cause sudden, severe visual loss due to retinal ischemia. The coronary arteries are often described as functional end arteries because they have anastomoses that may be insufficient to prevent ischemia during acute occlusion. The carotid and splenic arteries have significant collateral/anastomotic circulation and are not classic true end arteries. Hence, the retinal artery is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • True end artery → central retinal artery

  • Functional end arteries → coronary arteries

  • Retinal artery occlusion → acute retinal ischemia and severe visual loss

  • End artery → artery with no effective anastomosis

Exam Pearl: Central retinal artery = classic true end artery.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৯) Which is not one of the five components of protoplasm?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The classical five major components of protoplasm are water, proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and inorganic salts/electrolytes. These components collectively form the structural and functional basis of living cells. Vitamins are essential micronutrients involved mainly as coenzymes or regulatory molecules, but they are not considered one of the five major components of protoplasm in the conventional classification used in basic medical physiology. Therefore, vitamin is the correct answer. Electrolytes, including sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride, and phosphate, are included among the inorganic constituents of protoplasm.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Five major components → water, protein, lipid, carbohydrate, electrolytes

  • Water → largest component

  • Protein → major structural/functional component

  • Lipids → membranes and energy storage

  • Electrolytes → osmotic and electrical functions

Exam Pearl: Vitamin is not one of the five classical major components of protoplasm.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯০) Which is not allowed in acetylcholine gated channel?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) is a ligand-gated, non-selective cation channel. When acetylcholine binds, the channel opens and permits mainly Na⁺ and K⁺ to pass; some nicotinic receptor subtypes can also conduct Ca²⁺. Cl⁻, being an anion, is not conducted through the typical acetylcholine-gated nicotinic channel. The resulting inward positive current, predominantly due to Na⁺ entry, produces depolarization of the postsynaptic membrane. This mechanism is important at the neuromuscular junction and in autonomic ganglia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nicotinic ACh receptor → ligand-gated cation channel

  • Allows → Na⁺, K⁺

  • Some subtypes → Ca²⁺

  • Does not allow → Cl⁻

  • Net effect → depolarization

Exam Pearl: Nicotinic ACh channel conducts cations, not Cl⁻.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯১) ‘Cartwheel’ appearance of nucleus is characteristics of which stage?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The “cartwheel” or “clock-face” chromatin pattern is characteristic of the early normoblast (basophilic erythroblast) stage of erythropoiesis. At this stage, the nucleus contains coarse, deeply basophilic chromatin arranged in a spoke-like or cartwheel pattern. As erythroid maturation progresses, chromatin becomes increasingly condensed and the nucleus becomes smaller. In the intermediate normoblast (polychromatophilic erythroblast), the cytoplasm becomes grayish due to increasing hemoglobin, while the late normoblast (orthochromatic erythroblast) has a very condensed, pyknotic nucleus that is eventually extruded. Pronormoblasts have relatively fine, open chromatin.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pronormoblast → fine, open chromatin

  • Early/basophilic normoblast → cartwheel chromatin

  • Intermediate/polychromatophilic normoblast → gray-blue cytoplasm

  • Late/orthochromatic normoblast → pyknotic nucleus

  • Nucleus is ultimately extruded before reticulocyte stage

Exam Pearl: Cartwheel/clock-face chromatin = early (basophilic) normoblast.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯২) The RMP in neuron is---?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The resting membrane potential (RMP) of a typical neuron is approximately −70 mV. It results primarily from the unequal distribution of ions across the neuronal membrane, particularly the high intracellular concentration of K⁺ and the selective permeability of the resting membrane to K⁺ through leak channels. The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase maintains these ionic gradients by pumping 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ into the cell. The resting membrane is therefore electrically negative inside relative to the extracellular fluid. The exact RMP varies among neurons, but −70 mV is the standard exam value. −90 mV is closer to the equilibrium potential of K⁺ rather than the typical neuronal RMP.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Neuronal RMP → approximately −70 mV

  • Inside of neuron → negative

  • Major contributor → K⁺ leak

  • Na⁺/K⁺ pump → 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in

  • K⁺ equilibrium potential → approximately −90 mV

Exam Pearl: Neuron RMP = −70 mV.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৩) In case of DC of WBC monocyte occupies---?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In a normal differential leukocyte count (DLC), monocytes normally constitute approximately 2–8% of circulating white blood cells. They are the largest normal circulating leukocytes and have abundant gray-blue cytoplasm with a kidney-shaped or horseshoe-shaped nucleus. Monocytes are part of the mononuclear phagocyte system and migrate into tissues, where they differentiate mainly into macrophages or dendritic cells. The other leukocyte percentages are useful for comparison: neutrophils are approximately 40–75%, lymphocytes 20–40%, eosinophils 1–6%, and basophils 0–1%, depending on the reference range.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Monocytes → 2–8%

  • Neutrophils → ~40–75%

  • Lymphocytes → ~20–40%

  • Eosinophils → ~1–6%

  • Basophils → ~0–1%

Exam Pearl: Monocyte in DLC = 2–8%.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৪) Cardiac output increased in which of the following?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cardiac output is increased in anemia because reduced hemoglobin concentration decreases the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood. To maintain adequate tissue oxygen delivery, the body compensates by increasing heart rate and stroke volume, resulting in a high-output state. Reduced blood viscosity in significant anemia may also decrease systemic vascular resistance, further contributing to increased cardiac output. In contrast, hypothyroidism generally reduces cardiac output. Hemorrhage causes reduced circulating blood volume and usually decreases cardiac output. Shock is generally characterized by inadequate tissue perfusion and reduced cardiac output, although some distributive states can initially have high or normal output.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anemia → high-output cardiac state

  • Mechanisms → ↑ HR, ↑ SV, ↓ systemic vascular resistance

  • Hyperthyroidism → ↑ cardiac output

  • Hypothyroidism → ↓ cardiac output

  • Hemorrhage → ↓ venous return → ↓ cardiac output

Exam Pearl: Anemia is a classic cause of high-output cardiac failure.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৫) What is the capillary pressure (mm Hg) at venous end of capillary?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Capillary hydrostatic pressure falls from about 30–35 mmHg at the arterial end to approximately 10–15 mmHg at the venous end, depending on the reference used. However, in many physiology MCQs, the commonly taught value for the venous end is about 10 mmHg. Therefore, among the given options, গ) 10 mmHg is the expected answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Arterial end of capillary → ~30–35 mmHg

  • Venous end → ~10–15 mmHg

  • Capillary pressure progressively falls along the capillary

  • Lower venous-end pressure favors reduced filtration/reabsorption dynamics

Exam Pearl: For standard MCQs, remember capillary hydrostatic pressure ≈ 35 mmHg at arterial end and ≈ 10 mmHg at venous end.

So the best answer is: গ) 10 mmHg.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৬) How is the shape Oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve is __?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The oxyhemoglobin (oxygen–hemoglobin) dissociation curve has a characteristic sigmoid (S-shaped) appearance. This shape is mainly due to the cooperative binding of oxygen to hemoglobin. When one O₂ molecule binds to hemoglobin, the affinity of the remaining binding sites for O₂ increases. This produces a steep middle portion of the curve, allowing efficient oxygen loading in the lungs and unloading in tissues. Factors such as increased CO₂, H⁺, temperature, and 2,3-BPG shift the curve to the right, facilitating oxygen unloading.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve → Sigmoid / S-shaped

  • Cause → Cooperative O₂ binding

  • Right shift → ↑ CO₂, ↑ H⁺, ↑ temperature, ↑ 2,3-BPG

  • Right shift → increased O₂ unloading

  • Myoglobin curve → hyperbolic

Exam Pearl: Hemoglobin = sigmoid; myoglobin = hyperbolic.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৭) Which investigation is done to test filling of the bladder and bladder wall tone?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A cystometrogram (cystometry) is used to assess the filling phase of the urinary bladder, including bladder capacity, sensation, compliance, and detrusor (bladder wall) pressure/tone during filling. During the test, the bladder is gradually filled while intravesical pressure and sensations are recorded. It is particularly useful in evaluating neurogenic bladder and disorders of bladder storage or emptying.

  • USG → evaluates bladder anatomy, residual urine, stones, etc.

  • IVU → assesses the urinary tract using contrast imaging.

  • Cystoscopy → directly visualizes the bladder mucosa and urethra.

  • Cystometrogram → evaluates bladder filling and detrusor function.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bladder filling + pressure/tone → Cystometrogram

  • Bladder mucosa visualization → Cystoscopy

  • Residual urine → USG

  • Upper urinary tract contrast study → IVU

Exam Pearl: Cystometrogram = investigation of bladder capacity, sensation, compliance, and detrusor tone during filling.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৮) Which one does not increases thirst?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thirst is stimulated by increased plasma osmolality, angiotensin II, and dryness of the mouth. In contrast, increased blood pressure does not stimulate thirst; increased blood volume/pressure generally suppresses thirst by reducing renin and angiotensin II activity. The hypothalamic thirst center responds particularly to changes in plasma osmolality and circulating volume.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ↑ Osmolality → ↑ thirst

  • ↑ Angiotensin II → ↑ thirst

  • Dry mouth → ↑ thirst

  • ↑ Blood pressure/volume → ↓ thirst

Exam Pearl: Increased blood pressure is the odd one out—it does not increase thirst.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৯) Which muscle is attached to the head of the fibula?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The biceps femoris inserts mainly onto the head of the fibula. Its tendon can be palpated on the lateral side of the knee, and it is an important landmark around the fibular head. The biceps femoris is a hamstring muscle that flexes the knee and laterally rotates the leg when the knee is flexed.

The other options have different insertions:

  • Vastus lateralis → patella → tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament

  • Semitendinosus → upper medial tibia (pes anserinus)

  • Semimembranosus → posterior medial condyle of tibia

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Fibular head → Biceps femoris

  • Pes anserinus → Sartorius + Gracilis + Semitendinosus

  • Biceps femoris → lateral hamstring

  • Semitendinosus/Semimembranosus → medial hamstrings

Exam Pearl: Biceps femoris = insertion on the head of the fibula.

Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০০) Which hormone controls blood phosphate level?
Final Model Test-06 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is the major hormone regulating blood phosphate levels. PTH decreases phosphate reabsorption in the proximal renal tubules by downregulating Na⁺-phosphate cotransporters, thereby increasing phosphate excretion in urine (phosphaturia) and lowering serum phosphate. At the same time, PTH increases renal calcium reabsorption and stimulates activation of vitamin D, which increases intestinal calcium and phosphate absorption. Overall, the direct renal effect of PTH on phosphate is decreased serum phosphate.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PTH → ↓ serum phosphate

  • PTH → ↑ serum calcium

  • Kidney → ↓ phosphate reabsorption → phosphaturia

  • PTH stimulates renal 1α-hydroxylase → ↑ active vitamin D

  • ADH → water balance

  • Aldosterone → Na⁺/K⁺ balance

Exam Pearl: PTH is the key hormone controlling phosphate excretion and serum phosphate concentration.
